objective: Build the missing bottom-up bridge from a host-side robot command to a bounded, time-aligned, numerically valid, physically acknowledged MCU and drive execution path.

request_interpretation.curriculum_intent: Continue the robotics dependency graph after ROS 2 by owning the hardware-cycle assumptions that trajectory and feedback-control articles currently leave implicit.
request_interpretation.content_intent: Use one private compound failure to force coverage of command identity, latch deadlines, peripheral timing, NVIC/ISR/DMA, RTOS scheduling, blocking, fieldbus time, numeric bounds, and fault containment.
request_interpretation.visual_intent: Make every lab change a measurable physical or scheduling consequence rather than merely recoloring a diagram.
request_interpretation.paper_intent: Reconstruct Liu and Layland 1973 from its five assumptions through critical instants, rate-monotonic priority, utilization bounds, deadline-driven scheduling, mixed work, and author-stated limits.
request_interpretation.provenance_intent: Retain source, inclusion intent, boundary, public transformation, and QA repair decisions for later automatic knowledge compilation.
request_interpretation.small_model_intent: Keep decisions bounded enough for a 4B model to repair one formula or Viz and for a 9B model to assemble one causal section from source packets.

existing_coverage: robot-ros2-runtime-communication ends at a bounded host actuator callback
robot-dynamics-feedback-control computes u_k and assumes it is applied at the intended sample
signals-systems-convolution explains sampling and delay without mapping them to MCU peripherals
robot-ai-top-down names RTOS, CAN, EtherCAT, encoder, PWM, and FOC without their execution contract
gap_audit.scope_boundary: Motor electromagnetic equations, Clarke and Park transforms, FOC current regulation, inverter switching, sensing circuitry, thermal design, EMI, and PCB layout are reserved for the next motor-drive foundation.

source_decisions.source: Current FreeRTOS scheduling, interrupt, and mutex documentation
source_decisions.boundary: API behavior alone does not prove application schedulability, bound nested locks, or include device and bus delay.

source_decisions.source: Arm Cortex-M and NVIC official documentation
used_for: hardware priority before RTOS task scheduling
source_decisions.boundary: Implemented priority bits and numerical conventions vary by MCU and vendor.
The documented LET path does not automatically provide a fully implemented output-at-period-end physical latch contract.

source_decisions.source: EtherCAT Technology Group technology and implementation guides
source_decisions.boundary: Clock synchronization does not by itself bound application execution, driver response, cable faults, or achieved deployment accuracy.

source_decisions.source: C. L. Liu and James W. Layland, Scheduling Algorithms for Multiprogramming in a Hard-Real-Time Environment, JACM 1973
source_decisions.boundary: The theorems assume a single preemptive processor, independent periodic tasks, deadline equal to period, constant or maximum execution time, and restricted nonperiodic work; real MCU ISR, blocking, jitter, dependencies, I/O, cache, faults, and multicore require extensions.

private_transfer_gate.scenario: A six-axis manipulator receives 1 kHz EtherCAT torque commands while 20 kHz current, 2 kHz velocity, and 1 kHz outer loops run on Cortex-M. The link and heartbeat remain healthy while stale restart commands, software-skewed ADC reads, early DMA reuse, ISR logging, priority inversion, incomplete WCET, wrong timebase, timestamp wrap, fixed-point overflow, early watchdog kick, hidden driver trip, queued emergency traffic, and multi-axis late application interact.
private_transfer_gate.publication_policy: Do not publish the compound problem as a quiz. Require all sixteen premises to map to public derivation, formula, measured lab state, evidence slice, or operational gate.

source_extraction.paper: Liu and Layland 1973, Scheduling Algorithms for Multiprogramming in a Hard-Real-Time Environment
source_extraction.local_text_boundary: pdftotext and Python pypdf were unavailable, so no local text artifact was fabricated; the valid local PDF was retained and every page was read through the web PDF parser.
mechanism_notes: The paper states five simplifying assumptions before deriving scheduling results.
For fixed priorities, a task's critical instant occurs when it is released with all higher-priority tasks.
Rate monotonic is optimal among fixed-priority assignments under the stated model.
The m-task sufficient utilization bound is m times (2 to the power 1/m minus 1), approaching ln 2; exceeding it is inconclusive rather than automatic failure.
Deadline-driven scheduling reaches utilization one only under the paper's restricted model, not as practical 100 percent MCU headroom.
The paper discusses mixed scheduling and explicitly identifies periodicity and execution-time assumptions as limitations.

events.observed: The ROS 2 article could prove callback delivery while feedback control still assumed that u_k reached the plant on the intended hardware sample.
events.inference: The next prerequisite had to own host-to-MCU-to-power causality before adding a deeper motor-control algorithm.
events.decision: Implement embedded real-time execution now and reserve FOC, inverter, and PCB physics for the next milestone.

events.observed: Liu-Layland's well-known bounds are often quoted without the five assumptions that make them true.
events.inference: Publishing only U and ln 2 would teach unsafe transfer to modern firmware.
events.decision: Place assumptions before every theorem use, distinguish sufficient from necessary, and separate the paper's EDF result from practical headroom.

verification.expected: Readers can say when each theorem cannot be applied

events.observed: A summary would hide the proof environment, sufficient-versus-necessary distinction, mixed scheduling, and stated limitations needed to reproduce the paper responsibly.

implementation_decisions: Treat a setpoint as meaning, identity, target time, validity, fallback, and applied acknowledgement rather than a scalar payload.
Define real time at the physical PWM latch or fault consequence, not function return or average duration.
Use a peripheral timer as the sample-compute-actuate origin and separate acquisition skew from task jitter.
Model DMA as an explicit ownership state transition and keep ISR work bounded.
Teach utilization as load and a theorem certificate only under its assumptions, never as a universal response proof.
Put resource blocking into response analysis and compare inheritance, ceiling-like ownership, and redesign choices.
Separate link health, frame arrival, synchronized target cycle, command freshness, and multi-axis actuation evidence.
Treat timer arithmetic, numeric saturation, stack, logging, and allocation as real-time safety contracts.
Require independent hardware trip, firmware latch, host observation, and supervised reset to agree before power returns.
Put Korean operation rationale inside every display formula and keep detailed symbols, units, assumptions, and failure boundaries in FormulaNote.
Use semantic color, restrained line weights, stable card geometry, and red only for violated invariants.
Defer continuous animation until static interaction, responsive fit, and causal legibility pass.
